# Bundle sizes: vapor-chamber v1.35.0

All numbers are **minified, comment-free brotli** of what a consumer ships: a Vite production
build of each built export (`process.env.NODE_ENV` defined, minified, `vue` external - so dev-only
diagnostics fold away as they do in an app build), the pre-minified `.min.js` for IIFE, then
brotli q=11. Regenerated by `npm run size:doc`, verified fresh in CI. **Hard
ceilings apply to three measures only**: the IIFE variants (`scripts/check-size.mjs`), the typical
Blade consumer (tests/esm-treeshake.test.ts) and the Vapor outlet's own arm in an app build
(tests/vapor/vapor-outlet-size.test.ts). The ESM rows below are measured and published every run,
but nothing fails a build when one grows.

## ESM subpath exports

Each row is the cost of importing **only that export**, bundled self-contained with `vue`
external. **Read this carefully:** the shared command-bus core (6.1 KB brotli on its own) is
included in *every* row, so the rows are **not additive** - importing two exports does not cost
their sum (the core is shared once). `.` is the full main barrel measured *import-everything*;
your app's tree-shaking drops whatever you don't use (e.g. importing just `createCommandBus`
from it is 6.1 KB brotli, not 48.5 KB).

**brotli vs first load.** `brotli` joins every chunk of the build into one measurement, the
historical figure and the one to compare against older releases. `first load` and `on demand`
split the same chunks by reachability: a module behind an `import()` is its own chunk, and only
the chunks the entry reaches through static imports count as startup cost. **`first load` is
what a consumer downloads to start; `on demand` is fetched only if that feature is used.**
A `-` means nothing is deferred, which is every export except `./vitest` and `./router`. No row here is budgeted - see the note above.

## Vapor wiring, Vue bundled

The only rows with `vue` **bundled**, so a static Vue import shows its cost. The first row is a
hand-wired minimum: `createVaporApp` from `vue`, handed to `configureVue`, with the composables
from `vapor-chamber/vue`. Each row after it is the **difference from the row above** - what
`vapor-chamber/vapor` adds over hand-wiring (it wires `defineVaporComponent` and
`defineVaporAsyncComponent` as well), then each of the two names it leaves out, wired by hand.
The split was decided on the same measurement taken on the vapor-sfc example at rc.6
(src/vapor.ts); these rows re-take it from `dist/` on every run.

| step (rows after the first are deltas) | min KB | brotli KB |
|---|--:|--:|
| `Vapor wiring: hand-wired createVaporApp` | 47.9 | 16.3 |
| `vapor-chamber/vapor over that` | 4.4 | 1.4 |
| `+ defineVaporCustomElement` | 6.9 | 1.9 |
| `+ vaporInteropPlugin` | 73.0 | 23.1 |

## Example snippets

One row per top-level `examples/*.ts` (found by glob), each bundled the way the ESM rows are: a
Vite production build of the file itself, `vue` external, DEV folded. The row is the snippet's
own code plus the part of the library it imports. The Vite apps report their own `vite build`
sizes. Left out: `feature-vite-hmr.ts` (a Vite config that imports vite, not a browser bundle); `feature-vite-wire.ts` (a Vite config that imports vite and @vitejs/plugin-vue, not a browser bundle); `pattern-2-laravel-vite.ts` (imports App.vue, a page the repo does not carry); `pattern-3-inertia.ts` (imports @inertiajs/vue3 and page files the repo does not carry); `pattern-4-nextjs.tsx` (a React file, and the repo has no React); `pattern-6-vapor-router.ts` (imports .vue pages the repo does not carry); `vite.base.ts` (the shared Vite config of the Vue apps, not a browser bundle).
